cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Credit for the Discovery
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you lead tomorrow's house tour, explain that my diagram located the hidden doorway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to say Mum uncovered it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She uncovered the bricks. I identified the doorway. Please don't merge the investigation with the plaster removal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can open the door yourself. Everyone will see you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They'll see someone opening a door. Say who found it before I turn the handle.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks that a diagram's discovery be named. A3 corrects B2's merged uncovering/identification claim; A5 corrects B4's visibility offer into spoken attribution.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 proposes credit for Mum's uncovering, so A3 separates labor from identification. B4 offers opening the door, leading A5 to distinguish being seen from being credited.

relationship.evidence: B2 values Mum's work and B4 tries to include A visibly, making B a practical tour organizer rather than an opponent constructed for A's ego.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's public role as a deadline for acknowledgment: name the discovery before A turns the handle.

specificity.evidence: A1 tomorrow's house tour and hidden doorway, A3 plaster removal and B4 opening demonstrate the dispute without unseen discovery footage.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's two short sentences correct B's actual assumption about visibility; neither gives a thematic lesson about credit.
